candidates.title: Turn monthly review decks into video drafts

demandEvidence.chore: Prepare a narrated video draft from a monthly business review deck for its intended audience.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: if you send your team, your investors or your clients a review deck every month

ease.reason: The retained post gives an importable n8n workflow and setup steps, though API keys and file setup are required.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: consultants or small firms may pay for recurring report-to-video preparation; this post only offers a template.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can use synthetic reports and a proposed draft workflow; rendering setup and costs need checking.

autonomy.reason: The documented workflow runs report-to-video steps, but a person supplies files and keys and checks the render.

evidence.reason: The retained spans describe a monthly deck, setup, and reported rendering process; this is one maker's account.

candidates.reason: Concrete chore assessed as a narrow proposed experiment; its provisional five-criterion mean is below 6, so it is not proposed for publication.

experimentPlan.output: A reviewable narrated video draft based on a supplied monthly review deck.
inputs: Audience and company details supplied by an operator
Test API keys in a sandbox
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator places a synthetic monthly report in a test folder and starts a run.
steps: Read the supplied report and operator-entered audience details.
Draft a short narration and scene outline from the report.
Prepare a video render using a test account and provided credentials.
Return the render and source report for comparison.
Flag missing values or failed rendering for human review.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: A reviewer checks whether the draft mentions the report’s key figures accurately and whether every scene traces to supplied content.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies the report, audience, brand details, and authorized test credentials; they verify figures, approve the narration, and decide whether to share the video.
unverified: Reliability of report parsing across layouts
Actual API costs and account access
Whether the draft preserves all material figures
Suitability of the reported runtime for other inputs

candidates.title: Plan merchant interviews from app feedback

demandEvidence.chore: Help an app developer organize outreach and interview notes to learn how merchants work and where they struggle.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: finding store owners to talk to

ease.reason: A beginner can organize operator-supplied merchant feedback, but finding willing store owners remains manual.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: Shopify app developers may pay for better merchant research; the post establishes no purchase intent.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can classify fictional interview notes and draft outreach; participant recruitment and response remain uncertain.

autonomy.reason: A model can group supplied notes, but a person must recruit, conduct interviews, and validate themes.

evidence.reason: The retained post directly says developer responses are mostly partners and they want merchant perspectives; frequency is unclear.

candidates.reason: Concrete chore assessed as a narrow proposed experiment; its provisional five-criterion mean is below 6, so it is not proposed for publication.

experimentPlan.output: A short, reviewable summary of merchant needs from consented interview notes.
inputs: A list of app questions supplied by the developer
experimentPlan.trigger: After an app developer supplies test interview notes for review.
steps: Remove personal details from the synthetic notes.
Group comments under the supplied app questions.
Draft a short summary with supporting note snippets.
Flag questions with no matching comments.
Ask a person to review themes before outreach or product decisions.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: A reviewer verifies each summary point against a supplied note and confirms unsupported themes are marked as unknown.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person must recruit and speak with merchants, obtain permission, supply notes, and decide what to do; the experiment does not find participants.
unverified: Whether synthetic notes reflect real merchant language
Whether developers will pay for research support
Whether grouping is reliable across interview formats

candidates.title: Review Shopify tax exemption records

demandEvidence.chore: Prepare a human-reviewed checklist of product-specific exemption cases that need tax-rule confirmation before checkout.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Calculate the correct tax amounts before payment, without requiring draft orders, manual adjustments or additional invoices

ease.reason: A checklist prototype is possible, but no implementation reference documents Shopify tax rules or exemption behavior.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: merchants may pay to reduce manual exemption handling; this feature request proves no purchase or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week fictional-record checklist is bounded; correct tax treatment and Shopify integration are unsupported and excluded.

autonomy.reason: The proposed tool only flags cases for review; a qualified person must determine tax treatment and update records.

evidence.reason: The request explicitly names pre-payment tax calculation, GST/PST records, and manual workarounds, but no corroboration.

candidates.reason: Concrete chore assessed as a narrow proposed experiment; its provisional five-criterion mean is below 6, so it is not proposed for publication.

experimentPlan.output: A review queue that flags missing tax-rule decisions for a human before checkout.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator enters a fictional checkout case for review.
steps: Compare the case with operator-entered rule notes.
Flag missing or conflicting information without calculating tax.
Show the relevant note and case fields together.
Record the reviewer’s decision in a test-only table.
Return unresolved cases for qualified review.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: A qualified reviewer confirms each flag matches the supplied rule note and that no tax amount is calculated or presented as authoritative.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A qualified tax professional supplies and approves rules; a human handles every real transaction. No automated tax advice, calculation, checkout change, or invoice persistence is proposed.
unverified: Whether the operator-provided rule notes are complete
Shopify data access and record-writing behavior

candidates.title: Turn rough sketches into wireframe drafts

demandEvidence.chore: Create a reviewable digital wireframe draft from an operator-supplied rough sketch.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: translate rough sketches on my iPad to higher fidelity wireframes or illustrations in near real time

ease.reason: A mock can start from supplied sketches, but no supplied source documents an image-to-wireframe method.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent designers may pay to speed up wireframe drafting; the request does not show a buyer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week prototype can compare a few synthetic sketches with drafts, but fidelity and tool access are unknown.

autonomy.reason: A person must supply sketches, correct layout interpretation, and approve all generated design elements.

evidence.reason: The Ask HN post states the specific sketch-to-wireframe task but gives no examples, constraints, or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Concrete chore assessed as a narrow proposed experiment; its provisional five-criterion mean is below 6, so it is not proposed for publication.

experimentPlan.output: A low-fidelity wireframe draft with uncertain regions marked for designer review.
experimentPlan.trigger: A designer uploads a synthetic sketch and describes its intended screen.
steps: Read the supplied screen purpose and sketch.
List visible regions and labels with uncertainty markers.
Create a simple wireframe draft from the operator-confirmed list.
Compare the draft against the sketch and flag ambiguous regions.
Return the draft for designer correction.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: A designer checks that each draft element corresponds to a visible sketch element or is explicitly marked as an uncertain proposal.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A designer supplies the sketch, confirms interpretation, and approves the output; the experiment does not promise production-ready illustrations.
unverified: Availability and suitability of a wireframe generation tool

candidates.title: Scope a MirrorFly and n8n integration

demandEvidence.chore: Prepare a feasibility brief for a proposed MirrorFly-to-n8n workflow using operator-supplied events and fields.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want to check the possibility of integrating MirrorFly with n8n and understand how the platforms could work.

ease.reason: A beginner can map a few supplied requirements, but no API or webhook capability reference is attached.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: professional service operators may pay for integration scoping; this request establishes no purchase or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can produce a feasibility memo from fictional requirements, while actual API access and compatibility remain unknown.

autonomy.reason: The proposed output is a human-reviewed analysis; no integration execution is documented or proposed.

evidence.reason: The retained post explicitly asks about connecting MirrorFly and n8n, but gives examples rather than a chosen event or field map.

candidates.reason: The request supports a bounded feasibility brief, but its provisional five-criterion mean is below 6; no integration is proposed.

experimentPlan.output: A reviewable feasibility brief mapping one proposed communication event to an n8n workflow.
inputs: Operator-supplied desired CRM or notification outcome
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies a fictional event and describes the intended workflow outcome.
steps: List required event fields and the desired result.
Compare the supplied documentation with each required field.
Mark unsupported or undocumented steps as unknown.
Draft a proposed n8n flow using only confirmed fields.
Return questions and risks for a human integrator.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: A reviewer checks every mapped field against the supplied documentation and confirms unknown API behavior is clearly marked.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: An integrator supplies authorized documentation and validates the mapping; this plan does not connect accounts, call an endpoint, or prove that either product supports the integration.
unverified: MirrorFly API and webhook availability for the intended event
n8n connector or HTTP configuration needed
